exercise2.hint: A one-line summary is a start, not the whole thing. The exercise asks for three pieces: what it does, what each parameter is, and what comes back.

choices: On the line above the def
As the first statement inside the function body
At the very end of the function
Anywhere, as long as it uses triple quotes
questions.explain: Python keeps the first string in a function body as its documentation. A string anywhere else is just a string, and a line above the def is outside the function entirely.

questions.prompt: Which built-in shows you a function's documentation?
questions.explain: help() prints the signature and the docstring, which is why writing one pays off for anyone reading your code later, including you.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between a comment and a docstring?
choices: A comment is discarded when the code is parsed; a docstring stays attached to the function
A docstring is discarded; a comment stays
questions.explain: The parser throws comments away, so nothing can read them back. A docstring becomes the function's __doc__ and is what help() prints.

questions.prompt: What should a docstring for a function say?
choices: Every line of the implementation, restated
questions.explain: A docstring is for the person calling the function, so it describes the deal on offer. Restating the body helps nobody and goes stale the first time the body changes.

questions.prompt: A docstring is written between triple ___ marks.
questions.explain: Three quote marks let the string run over several lines, which is why docstrings use them even when they are short.
